scope: Offline Silero speech-mask diagnostic, never applied by the app. No new dependency or model threshold tuning.

plan.candidate: Intersect unchanged diarization turns with the existing Silero speech regions, using the existing 200 ms per-region margin; keep unknown identities, source time and overlap. No audio concatenation or label changes.
plan.selection: Prior four human first-120-second clips plus the same six controlled quiet/noise/echo transforms; new TS3003a first120 is chosen before candidate output as a recording-disjoint diagnostic evaluation. Add a 200 ms public-domain speech excerpt at 2 s in a 10 s silence control.
plan.acceptance: False alarms and DER must not increase, missed speaker-ms must not increase, and no previously covered reference turn (especially <=250 ms) may lose all activity on any case. No threshold or margin sweep. Reject general filtering if any check fails.
plan.scope: Offline diagnostic only. Known sources and transformed variants are calibration; TS3003a is new to this experiment, but model/speaker-training independence is not established. No independent Portuguese human evaluation or app activation.

priorStressRecipe.purpose: Controlled calibration stress diagnostics, not independent human evaluation or physical device validation.

noise.rms: whole source mono PCM RMS, not speech-only RMS

priorStressRecipe.reference: Original anonymous intervals propagated to the transformed source clock; echo adds a same-speaker copy shifted by 200 ms and clipped at 120000 ms. Mark annotation controlled and split calibration. No waveform speech realignment or human reannotation.
priorStressRecipe.format: Canonical PCM16 mono WAV, original sample rate; stereo averaged before transformation; round to nearest integer ties even and clamp to [-32768,32767].
priorStressRecipe.acceptance: Diagnostic only. Compare against reconstructed former 17-ms gap filling; no tuning or activation from these controls.

limitations: Known clips and controlled transforms are calibration; only TS3003a is a new recording for this experiment. Speaker identity and model-training independence are not established.
No independent Portuguese human evaluation source or physical microphone/system echo/alignment acceptance.
Short control is a controlled 200 ms fragment, not a human-annotated complete word. Other short-turn checks use supplied reference intervals.

Silero inference cannot abort mid-call. Diagnostic admission waits behind interactive work; its whole-source bounded native call holds the scheduler slot and is not a production preemption implementation.
Model paths must be trusted and immutable during use; Linux keeps the verified descriptor through native loading and detects persistent edits by rehashing. This is not an immutable snapshot.
Masking speech cannot fix speaker identity merges or excess overlapping voices while speech continues.
Missed time follows the supplied references: C-ORAL utterance intervals include pauses. Its extra missed time alone does not prove loss of phonetic content; acoustic validation remains open.
decision: Reject general speech masking: at least one frozen no-regression/short-speech gate failed. Keep the diagnostic opt-in only; do not change the app or baseline diarization.
